# Madison Good Neighbor Gathering

## What is it?

The Madison Good Neighbor Gathering is a free annual outdoor community festival on Madison's near west side. Over 700 neighbors attended last year. It brings together families to celebrate the diverse cultures, music, dance, and spirit of Madison's neighborhoods. The event is organized by neighbors, for neighbors: no tickets, no registration, just show up and have fun.

## 2027 Event Details

- **Date:** Not announced yet. The 2027 date will be posted here and on Instagram once it is set. It lands on a Sunday afternoon in early fall; 2026 was Sunday, September 13.
- **Time:** 12:00 PM – 4:00 PM (CDT) in past years
- **Location:** Brittingham Park, 829 W. Washington Ave., Madison, WI 53715
- **Admission:** Free to enter, and every activity is free. Food carts and the makers market are local small businesses selling their own food and goods, so those are not free.
- **Weather:** Event cancelled only for severe weather; check Instagram for updates

## Activities (based on past years, 2027 lineup TBA)

- Bouncy structures and inflatables
- Rock climbing wall
- Science & Discovery with Wisconsin Science Festival and Dane County Trash Lab
- Madison Children's Museum interactive play
- Vilas Zoo live animal ambassadors
- Community resource tables (local organizations, services, programs)
- Free family portrait photos against a colorful backdrop

## Entertainment / Performances (the 2026 schedule, as an example of the shape of the day)

- Taiko Performance — Japanese Drumming (12:00 PM)
- Welcome / Opening Remarks (12:30 PM)
- Hmong Dancers — Traditional Dance (12:45 PM)
- Rael The Artist — Live Music (1:00 PM)
- Ballet — Dance Performance (2:00 PM)
- Juggler — Family Entertainment (3:00 PM)
- Francis Medrano — Afro-Peruvian Dance Party (3:30 PM)
- End of event (4:00 PM)

## Food & Vendors

- Multiple local food carts on-site with diverse, family-friendly options. Food is for purchase, not free.
- A makers market of Madison artists and small businesses selling their own goods
- Cash and card accepted
- No outside food restrictions, picnics welcome
- No alcohol served (alcohol-free event)

## Getting There

- **By car:** Free street parking on surrounding streets (can fill on nice days)
- **By bus:** Metro Transit has several routes nearby
- **By bike:** Very bike-friendly; BCycle docking stations close to the park
- **Accessibility:** Brittingham Park has paved paths throughout; stroller and wheelchair accessible

## Organizers

- **Neighborhood House Community Center** — serving Madison families since 1916 with youth programs, adult education, a food pantry, and more. [neighborhoodhousemadison.org](https://www.neighborhoodhousemadison.org)
- **New Culture Church** — an authentic faith community welcoming to questioners, newcomers, and anyone who doesn't have it all figured out. [newculturechurch.com](https://newculturechurch.com)
- **District 13 Neighborhood Associations** — six neighborhood associations uniting to celebrate and strengthen the community.
- **Triangle Ministries** — serving residents of Madison's Triangle Neighborhood since 1978 with holistic health services, food programs, and community-building support. [trianglecommunityministry.org](https://trianglecommunityministry.org)
- **UnityPoint Health – Meriter** — a UW Health partner providing personal, community-centered care in Madison. [unitypoint.org](https://www.unitypoint.org)
- **Bayview Foundation** — affordable housing and supportive community services for culturally diverse, low-income Madison families since 1966. [bayviewfoundation.org](https://bayviewfoundation.org)

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is it really free?**
Yes — no tickets, no registration, no hidden fees. Just show up.

**How many people come?**
Over 700 neighbors attended last year.

**What should I bring?**
A blanket for sitting on the lawn, sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and cash or card for food vendors.

**Can I bring my dog?**
Yes! Dogs on a leash are welcome. Please clean up after them.

**Is there an ATM?**
No ATM on site. Bring cash if you plan to purchase food, or use a card.

**Is it accessible?**
Yes — paved paths throughout, accessible for strollers, wheelchairs, and mobility devices.
